parole.significato: alto (musical voice; person or instrument that performs the alto part)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian alto from Latin altus. Doublet of alt.

parole.significato: raised deck or terrace, large balcony supported by walls or columns
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian altana (15th century).

parole.significato: aria (solo singing piece, notably in operatic genres)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian aria, from Latin āēr (“air (atmosphere), breath”).
Borrowed from Italian arpeggio.

parole.significato: artichoke (edible plant related to the thistle)
parole.testo: From Northern Italian articiocco, from Provençal archichaut, arquichaut, from Old Spanish alcarchofa, from Andalusian Arabic الْخَرْشُوف (al-ḵaršūf), from Arabic الْخُرْشُوف (al-ḵuršūf), definite form of خُرْشُوف (ḵuršūf).

parole.significato: assassin (member of the historical Ismaili Muslim militant group)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian assassino.
Borrowed from Italian assicuranza.

parole.significato: a public celebration with honking cars driving in a row; on any occasion, but commonest with weddings and football vict…
parole.testo: From Auto (“car”) + Korso (“celebratory row of vehicles”). The latter from Italian corso in the archaic sense of “horse race” (for which now corsa). In German, the word is chiefly used in compounds.

parole.significato: A notification or announcement, usually written, especially of a shipment sent to the recipient
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian avviso, from Old French avis.

parole.significato: comic figure or buffoon in Italian theater
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian pagliaccio.

parole.significato: canopy, dais, baldaquin (ornamental roof over an altar, throne, bed etc.)

parole.significato: ladyfinger (A small sponge cake, shaped approximately like a finger)

parole.significato: forepaw of an animal (e.g. wild ones like lion and bear, but also of tamed ones like dog and cat)

Borrowed from Italian catenaccio.

18th century, from Italian dilettante.

parole.significato: to dabble (to participate in an artistic activity without the necessary skills)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian dilettare (“to please”), with -ieren.
Borrowed from Italian disconto, older form of sconto.

parole.significato: an inexperienced person acting as experienced

parole.significato: corsair, pirate (one who plunders at sea) (of male or unspecified sex)

parole.significato: skirt suit (women’s business suit consisting of a skirt and jacket)
